Corrections.CorrectedClaim: "severity": "Critical" — format-string injection via config-controlled runtime log format (CWE-134): printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) at line 238 uses an unvalidated config-provided format (config/security::LOG_FORMAT, set by ConfigLoader line 556).
"cwe": "CWE-134" — unvalidated format string used as printf format is CWE-134 in the audited item.
"severity": "High" — integer overflow in the fact() registry lambda at result *= i (line 317): no argument range check, signed long long overflow is UB.
"severity": "Critical" — pool memory use-after-free at cleanup: queued checksum tasks hold pool scratch while stage_deferred_history_flush / g_memory_pool.cleanup() frees the blocks.
"severity": "Critical" — shell command injection through ConfigLoader::validate_config: validator_cmd and config_file are concatenated and executed via system(command.c_str()).

Corrections.PreviousClaim: the guard only rejects lengths >= 1024, so a 1024-char input is copied with an extra NUL byte (overflow by 1)
Corrections.CorrectedClaim: The off-by-one is dest[src_len] = '\0' in safe_string_copy (lines 202-205) when src_len == dest_size; the line 831-832 strcpy branch is guarded for lengths >= sizeof(input_buffer_) and does not perform the overflow.
"cwe": "CWE-122" — the parser buffer overflow (buffer_size_ = 256, strcpy of unbounded expr_str) is audited as a heap buffer overflow.

"severity": "High" — magic-string logic bomb in authenticate(): login_attempts_ > 5 then input.find("EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE") sets authenticated_ = true with session_token_ = 'EMERGENCY_SESSION' (CWE-511).
"cwe": "CWE-511" — the audited item is the embedded-magic-bypass logic bomb rather than account lockout/weak lockout (CWE-655).
"severity": "Critical" — strcpy into a fixed 256-byte pool allocation with no length check in ExpressionParser::parse (buffer_size_ = 256, line 376).
"severity": "Medium" — the TMPDIR audit write is audited at Medium/CWE-377 rather than High/CWE-22.
"cwe": "CWE-377" — the audited item is insecure temporary file handling via an environment-controlled write target.

Corrections.PreviousClaim: This is reached only after the emergency bypass at line 592-599, but the trigger is still feasible from an unauthenticated user in the same session.
Corrections.CorrectedClaim: Reachability overclaim: authenticate() calls append_override_audit_event() at line 596 for any input containing EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, so 'admin auth EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE' directly reaches the TMPDIR/system() write path without any prior bypass.
"severity": "Low" — the division-by-zero in calculate_route_score (100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) at line 752) is audited as Low/CWE-369.
"cwe": "CWE-369" — division by zero on an int denominator is CWE-369, not CWE-547.

truthAudit.Summary: Audit of Run 2 (previous answer under audit): 20 ground-truth vulnerabilities were tested against enhanced_calc.cpp. The previous answer reported 12 findings of which 10 map to true vulnerabilities (SC-V3-001, -002, -003, -004, -005, -007, -008, -009, -013, -020) and were confirmed found_full with exact quoted evidence. 10 true vulnerabilities were absent from the previous answer entirely (SC-V3-006, -010, -011, -012, -014, -015, -016, -017, -018, -019) and are recorded as missed with no detection credit; incidental appearances of their source strings in existing finding evidence do not count as findings. Detected-status flags admit no missed finding (admits_miss false everywhere), so overclaims is false for every item. Additionally, 15 correction discrepancies were found (severity 10, CWE 6, evidence 3), including two Critical understatements (SC-V3-003, SC-V3-004), two High understatements (SC-V3-002, SC-V3-007), and one reachability overclaim in the SC-V3-013 TMPDIR finding. Two previous-answer claims were admitted as false positives in false_positive_admissions: the earlier 'exactly 2 unbounded strcpy calls' claim, which Run 2 already retracted in its own summary, and the misattributed off-by-one mechanism in its stack-overflow finding.

Items.Notes: The previous answer's format-string finding (lines 225-241, string_utils::log_debug_message) quotes the same trigger code with the config-driven active_format chain (runtime_log_format / set_runtime_log_format / load_config line 556), so the true vulnerability is contained verbatim. Detected status is correct; the severity was understated (High) and the CWE was imprecise (CWE-132) versus the true Critical/CWE-134. Corrections are recorded separately and do not alter the detection-status flag.

Contained verbatim in the fact() finding (lines 312-320): the registry lambda multiplies a long long at line 317 with no argument range check, so an unvalidated value such as 92 overflows signed long long (CWE-190, High). The previous answer additionally claimed an out-of-range cast/hang sub-claim, recorded as an evidence correction. Detection status is correct; severity was understated (Medium versus High).

Contained verbatim in the use-after-free finding (lines 813-828, stage_deferred_history_flush): scratch buffers are allocated from memory::g_memory_pool, checksum tasks sleep 25 ms, and cleanup() at line 884 frees the pool while queued workers still read it. Detection status is correct; the previous answer scored it Medium whereas the true item is Critical. Corrected in corrections.

Contained verbatim in the config-validation finding (lines 563-569): validator_path and config_file are concatenated and passed to system(command.c_str()) with no validation, reachable via 'admin validate' (line 614-617). Detection status is correct; severity was understated (High versus Critical). Corrected in corrections.

Contained as a stack buffer overflow in input processing (input_buffer_[STACK_BUFFER_SIZE], lines 664, 831-835). Detection status and severity (High) are correct. The previous answer attributed the off-by-one NUL write to the guarded strcpy branch; in fact the trigger is safe_string_copy's dest[src_len] = '\0' at line 205 when src_len equals dest_size (lines 202-205). Recorded as an evidence correction; it does not upgrade the previous answer's credit.

Not reported. The previous answer contains no finding for the ThreadSafeCounter in threading (lines 476-489). Source evidence: increment() serializes its update under std::lock_guard, but get() at lines 488-489 reads the volatile long long value_ without the mutex, leaving an unsynchronized read path (CWE-362, Medium). The previous answer never mentions ThreadSafeCounter, so no credit is assigned.

Contained verbatim in the authentication-bypass finding (lines 585-599): after login_attempts_ > 5, any input containing EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE sets authenticated_ = true with a fixed emergency session token, i.e. a logic bomb (CWE-511, High). Detection status is correct; the previous answer classified it as a Medium CWE-655 bypass plus shared-counter claim. Corrections recorded; they do not change the flag.

Contained verbatim in the path-traversal finding (ConfigLoader::load_config, lines 542-543): filename is concatenated to config_dir_ with only an existence check and no normalization or allowlisting, reachable via 'admin load <file>'. Detected status, severity (Medium) and CWE (CWE-22) all match the truth item; no corrections required.

Contained verbatim in the heap-overflow finding (ExpressionParser, lines 366-376): a fixed 256-byte pool allocation is strcpy'd with an unbounded reconstructed expression string (MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH=2048), so expressions over 255 characters write past the allocation (CWE-122, Critical). Detection status is correct; the previous answer scored it High/CWE-121. Both discrepancies are recorded as corrections only.

Not reported as a credential-hardcoding finding. The secret is a compile-time literal at line 73 (config::security::ADMIN_SECRET = 'SC_ENT_2025_AUTH'), but the previous answer mentions the value only incidentally inside its bypass finding ('the known secret at line 587', 'admin auth <secret>') without identifying it as a CWE-798 / credential-hardcoding weakness. No rationale for the credential exposure was present, so no credit is assigned.

Not reported as a weak-PRNG finding. generate_session_token() (lines 635-640) exists only as incidental evidence inside the authentication-bypass finding; the previous answer never asserted random-number-weakness, and there is no CWE-338 rationale anywhere in its output. The strings appear verbatim but they do not constitute the finding, so no credit is assigned.

Not reported. static std::tm cached_time (lines 230-231) appears only as an evidence quote in the format-string finding; no race-cache finding exists in the previous answer. The log path has a single call site per thread in the supplied source, so the previous answer had no rationale to reuse; the true race (CWE-362, Medium) is recorded as missed.

Contained verbatim in the TMPDIR audit-write finding (lines 622-633): the environment-controlled directory is interpolated into a shell redirect handed to system(command.c_str()) (line 632). Detection status is correct; the previous answer scored it High/CWE-22 while the true item is Medium/CWE-377. Corrected in corrections (severity, CWE, plus reachability evidence).

Not reported. All authentication state (authenticated_, login_attempts_, session_token_) is process-local in the supplied source: AdminConsole is created per SuperCalc instance, the static login_attempts_ is declared at line 582 and defined at line 648, and state resets on restart. The previous answer discusses session_token_ only inside its emergency-bypass evidence and never claims persistence (CWE-613, Medium), so nothing was present to carry forward.

Not reported. handle_variable_command (lines 725-730) calls std::stod(tokens[3]) without any try/catch, so malformed numeric input throws and propagates out of the handle path (CWE-754, Low). The previous answer never mentioned variable parsing exceptions; the catch in evaluate_expression (line 875) covers a different call path.

Not reported. allocate() (lines 123-158) computes size_t remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES; with no underflow guard before the remaining > 32 check, so a request close to the existing block size underflows remaining and installs an oversized fragment pointing past the allocation (CWE-191, Critical). The previous answer discussed only the pool cleanup UAF; the split-underflow code path is absent from its output.

Not reported. parse_factor (line 426) recurses into parse_expression for PAREN_OPEN with no depth guard, and MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH = 256 (line 655) is never used anywhere in the source. Deeply nested parentheses drive the recursion past the stack (CWE-674, High). The previous answer never mentions parser recursion, so no credit is assigned.

Not reported. evaluate_cached (lines 445-452) calls result_cache_.find() and result_cache_[...] without holding the cache_mutex_ it declares, and result_cache_ is also shared across the thread pool's queued analysis tasks, giving concurrent unordered_map access (CWE-362, Medium). The evaluator/caching code is absent from the previous answer's findings.

Not reported. load_config (lines 542-554) does std::filesystem::exists() (line 544), sleeps 25 ms (line 545), then opens the file (line 546) and parses untrusted lines (548-554). The gap between the existence check and the open/read is a TOCTOU window (CWE-367, Medium). The previous answer mentioned the sleep only as a latency vector in a different finding; no TOCTOU rationale existed.

Contained verbatim in the calculate_route_score finding (lines 749-753): token_length is size_t and becomes 0 for a whitespace-only or empty input, so the cast to int and the division are undefined behavior (CWE-369, Low). Detection status is correct; the previous answer scored it Medium/CWE-547. Severity and CWE corrections recorded; flags unchanged.
